subject: Discovery: Tool-calling & structured output for support automation
summary: Post-call recap confirming VertexAI Labs' support automation goals, current stack (Zendesk + internal microservices), success criteria (deterministic JSON output for downstream workflows), proposed JSON schema and next steps (follow-up PoC and SOW/contract intro).
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <alex@vertexailabs.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Sengupta <priya.s@vertexailabs.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery: Tool-calling & structured output for support automation

Jordan — thanks for the time today. Quick recap from our side to make sure we captured everything correctly: 

- Pain: Our support team spends ~40% of time triaging and formatting customer inputs before creating tickets in Zendesk; automations frequently fail because outputs aren't in a deterministic schema.
- Current stack: Zendesk for tickets, internal microservice (ticket-enricher) that enriches and routes tickets, and a small rules engine for SLA routing.
- Goal: Replace manual triage with a tool-calling agent that emits a strict JSON payload the ticket-enricher can consume reliably. Primary fields: intent, urgency_score, category, canonical_description, suggested_tags, related_docs.
- Success criteria: >=85% fidelity of generated JSON vs. human baseline; sub-200ms median extra latency for the agent step; smooth fallback to human when confidence < threshold.

Next steps from VertexAI Labs: share a sample of 250 anonymized support threads (we'll scrub PHI); get a proposed schema + quick PoC plan; align on SOW/contract and procurement timeline (we target pilot in Q3).

Thanks — Alex
Senior Product Manager
VertexAI Labs

---
(This message summarizes our notes from the 45-min discovery call earlier today.)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex@vertexailabs.com>
Cc: Priya Sengupta <priya.s@vertexailabs.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery: Tool-calling & structured output for support automation

Alex — really appreciated the conversation. Helpful to see how high the manual triage burden is. I’m capturing the items we discussed and a proposal for how Redwood can help: 

1) Pain & goals (short): eliminate manual formatting, produce deterministic JSON for downstream ticket-enricher, reduce time-to-resolution by routing more accurately.

2) Proposed approach: use a tool-calling agent that 1) classifies intent & category, 2) extracts canonical_description (cleaned customer text), 3) computes urgency_score and suggested_tags, and 4) returns a stable JSON schema that your microservice can validate. We'll implement prefix caching for common templates and a low-latency path to meet your 200ms target for the agent step.

3) JSON schema (attached): ri_tool_calling_json_schema_v1.json — key fields and deterministic constraints. Example (excerpt):
{
  "ticket_intent": "refund_request|bug_report|feature_request|other",
  "urgency_score": "0.0-1.0",
  "category": "billing|login|performance|ui|integration|other",
  "canonical_description": "string(<=2000)",
  "suggested_tags": "[string]",
  "confidence": "0.0-1.0"
}

Notes on deterministic formatting: we will enforce strict typing, canonical tokenization rules for descriptions (strip PII, normalize whitespace), and deterministic ordering for arrays (sort suggested_tags alphabetically) so your ticket-enricher has no ambiguity. We will also support a validation mode where Redwood returns both the JSON and a list of schema violations (if any) for the first 1000 messages in the pilot.

4) Success metrics & monitoring: we propose a small eval harness to measure fidelity vs. human-labeled ground truth (250 threads), latency histograms, and fallback rate by confidence threshold.

5) Next steps / asks:
- You to share the anonymized sample (250 threads) and a short list of priority categories by 2026-06-17.
- Redwood to deliver the attached schema + sample PoC plan (2-week PoC) and a rough cost estimate for pilot by 2026-06-19.
- Intro to procurement / legal for SOW on your side — we can loop in contracts when you’re ready.

I attached: ri_tool_calling_json_schema_v1.json (schema v1) and a short discovery-notes PDF. I’ve cc'ed Neha (solutions) and Marissa (AE) so we can scope the PoC and pricing. If this looks right, suggest a 30-min follow-up next Wed to align on data handoff.

—Jordan
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132
